title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper develops a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal performance with logarithmic regret.
motivation: Online learning of quantum states is crucial for adaptive quantum experiments and quantum machine learning, but existing methods suffer from linear regret or require strong assumptions.
method: The authors propose a Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) algorithm with a novel regularizer based on the von Neumann entropy, and analyze its regret using information-theoretic tools.
result: The algorithm achieves O(log T) regret for pure state tomography, matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to constant factors, and outperforms previous approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretically optimal and practical algorithm for online pure state learning, with implications for adaptive quantum information processing.

title: Gradiometric, Fully Tunable C-shunted Flux Qubits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a gradiometric, fully tunable C-shunted flux qubit design that reduces sensitivity to flux noise while maintaining wide tunability.
motivation: Flux qubits suffer from flux noise that limits coherence; a gradiometric design can cancel common-mode noise, but previous designs lacked tunability. The authors aim to combine noise immunity with full frequency tunability.
method: They introduce a C-shunted flux qubit with a gradiometric loop geometry, using a separate flux bias line for tuning, and characterize coherence times and tunability via microwave spectroscopy and time-domain measurements.
result: The qubit achieves coherence times exceeding 10 μs, with reduced sensitivity to global flux noise, and maintains tunability over several GHz.
conclusion: The gradiometric C-shunted flux qubit is a promising platform for scalable quantum processors, offering both noise resilience and operational flexibility.

title: Optimal Control For Rydberg Multi-qubit Operations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents optimal control techniques for multi-qubit operations in Rydberg atom arrays, achieving high-fidelity gates with reduced crosstalk.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but multi-qubit operations suffer from crosstalk and limited fidelity. Optimal control can mitigate these issues.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to design pulse sequences for Rydberg multi-qubit gates, using numerical optimization to minimize gate errors and crosstalk.
result: They demonstrate significant improvements in gate fidelity and reduction of crosstalk compared to standard approaches, enabling high-fidelity multi-qubit operations.
conclusion: Optimal control is an effective tool for enhancing Rydberg multi-qubit operations, bringing the platform closer to practical quantum computing.

title: Doubly-polylog-time-overhead Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation By A Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect Matching Decoder
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme with doubly polylog-time overhead using a polylog-time parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient decoding algorithms to correct errors with low time overhead, which is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The authors develop a parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder that runs in polylogarithmic time and integrate it into a fault-tolerant protocol achieving doubly polylogarithmic time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with time overhead scaling as O(polylog(n)) for both the decoder and the overall protocol, significantly improving over previous approaches.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible with efficient parallel decoding, advancing the practicality of large-scale quantum computing.

title: Magnon Fluctuations Find A Structure
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: Observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators driven into a non-equilibrium state.
motivation: To understand and control magnon fluctuations in non-equilibrium magnetic systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: Experimental observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators under non-equilibrium driving conditions.
result: Magnon fluctuations can be selectively redistributed via squeezing in non-equilibrium magnetic insulators.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum systems, with potential implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Exchange-mediated Spin–electric Control Of Single Molecules On Surfaces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: Exchange interactions enable electric control of single-molecule spins on surfaces, demonstrated for two molecular species.
motivation: Single molecules hosting isolated spins are promising for quantum technologies, but controlling them electrically is challenging; exchange interactions offer a new mechanism.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to probe and manipulate spin states of individual molecules on a surface, leveraging exchange coupling between the molecule and the substrate or between molecules.
result: They demonstrate that exchange interactions allow electric-field control of the spin state, achieving coherent manipulation and readout.
conclusion: Exchange-mediated spin-electric control provides a versatile tool for quantum control of molecular spins, relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum sensing.

title: Observation Of Non-adiabatic non-Abelian Braiding Of Matter Waves
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of non-adiabatic non-Abelian braiding using a Bose-Einstein condensate, simulating topological quantum computation.
motivation: Non-Abelian braiding is key for topological quantum computing, but adiabatic implementations are slow; this work aims to realize fast non-Abelian manipulation.
method: A Bose-Einstein condensate is used as a quantum simulator to implement non-adiabatic braiding operations of matter waves.
result: Successful observation of non-adiabatic non-Abelian braiding, enabling faster manipulation than adiabatic approaches.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates a viable platform for fast topological quantum operations, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enhancing Classical Simulation With Noisy Quantum Devices
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to enhance classical simulation of quantum circuits by leveraging noisy quantum devices, using a hybrid approach that combines noisy quantum outputs with classical post-processing.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is computationally expensive, and noisy quantum devices are imperfect but may still provide useful information to accelerate classical simulation.
method: The authors develop a protocol where a noisy quantum device is used to generate samples or expectation values, which are then fed into a classical algorithm to improve the accuracy of the simulation, possibly using error mitigation techniques.
result: The hybrid approach achieves better simulation accuracy than purely classical methods for certain circuit sizes and noise levels, demonstrating a practical advantage of noisy quantum devices.
conclusion: Noisy quantum devices can serve as useful resources for classical simulation, offering a new pathway to harness near-term quantum hardware for computational tasks.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: A context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, which is inaccurate for trapped-ion systems with non-Markovian effects, leading to unreliable characterization.
method: The authors develop a context-aware tomography protocol that models non-Markovian noise by incorporating temporal correlations and using a tensor network representation of the process.
result: The method yields more accurate and self-consistent estimates of gate fidelities and error rates compared to standard GST, demonstrated on simulated and experimental trapped-ion data.
conclusion: Accounting for non-Markovianity improves the reliability of quantum gate characterization, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with trapped ions.

title: A Framework Of Partial Error Correction For Intermediate-scale Quantum Computers
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a framework for partial error correction tailored to intermediate-scale quantum computers, balancing error suppression and resource overhead.
motivation: Full quantum error correction is too resource-intensive for near-term devices; partial error correction can improve fidelity with fewer qubits.
method: Develops a theoretical framework that interpolates between no error correction and full fault-tolerant correction, using code concatenation and flag qubits.
result: Demonstrates that partial error correction can significantly reduce logical error rates with moderate overhead, making it practical for NISQ-era devices.
conclusion: Partial error correction offers a viable path to enhance quantum computation on intermediate-scale hardware before full fault tolerance is achieved.

title: Planar Fault-tolerant Logical Measurements With Low Qubit Overhead
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method for fault-tolerant logical measurements on planar surface codes with reduced qubit overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant logical measurements are essential for quantum error correction, but existing methods require high qubit overhead. Reducing this overhead is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors propose a planar architecture for logical measurements that uses fewer ancilla qubits and simpler connectivity, leveraging lattice surgery and code deformation techniques.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves fault tolerance with significantly lower qubit overhead compared to standard approaches, while maintaining comparable error thresholds.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum error correction by enabling more resource-efficient logical operations, bringing fault-tolerant quantum computing closer to realization.

title: Harnessing Loss For Q-modulated Biosensors
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: A nanophotonic biosensor using radiative Q-factor modulation in a BIC metasurface for ultrasensitive detection of tumor extracellular vesicles.

method: Exploits bound states in the continuum (BIC) in a metasurface to convert refractive-index changes into large intensity variations via Q-factor modulation.
result: Demonstrates detection of tens of tumor extracellular vesicles within 15 minutes, with high sensitivity and scalability.
conclusion: The Q-modulated biosensing strategy offers a practical platform for point-of-care diagnostics with high sensitivity and speed.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;

method: The authors compare regression-based methods, network-based architectures, and decomposition techniques for discovering dynamical models from time-series data.
result: The review evaluates strengths, limitations, and complementarity of these approaches, providing a guide for selecting appropriate methods.
conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for biological modeling, but careful method selection is crucial based on data characteristics and system complexity.

title: Real-space Imaging Of The Electron-pair Density Hole In Molecular Auger–Meitner Decay

result: The experiment resolves the spatial redistribution of electrons, providing a direct image of the electron-pair density hole.

abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;

result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei provide enhanced sensitivity to certain symmetry-violating effects, making them promising for fundamental physics tests.

title: Visualizing Optical Anisotropy
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;

method: The authors develop a non-interferometric imaging framework that reconstructs the full dielectric tensor from intensity measurements, enabling volumetric characterization of anisotropy.
result: The framework enables quantitative 3D reconstruction of full dielectric tensors, allowing volumetric optical measurement of biaxial anisotropy in complex materials and biological structures.
conclusion: This approach opens a practical route to volumetric optical measurement of biaxial anisotropy, with potential applications in materials science and biology.
